title: Rosa's new car: Michigan auto laws, limits, proof and cancellation
summary: Follow Rosa's first year with her new car in Lansing: liability limits, proof, excluded and ride-share drivers, who pays PIP, the MAIPF and Chapter 32.
objectives: Know Michigan's default and lowest liability limits, and the limits before July 2, 2020
Spot who must carry no-fault, the penalties, special drivers and crash-parts rules
Find who pays PIP first, including in a short-term rental
Apply Chapter 32 cancellation and nonrenewal rules, and know the MAIPF

scenes.title: Rosa's limits: the Michigan defaults
scenes.src: MCL 500.3009(1),(5)-(8); DIFS FIS-PUB 6310; adapted from memory hook mn_auto-14; question auto-001
scenes.plain: The least a Michigan auto policy issued after July 1, 2020 may carry, unless the insured signs a form choosing lower injury limits.
scenes.example: Rosa's policy, issued in 2026, starts at the defaults: if she's sued for hurting three people in one crash, it pays at most $250,000 each, $500,000 in all.
scenes.exam: Lower injury limits need the DIFS form, never below $50,000 and $100,000. Before July 2, 2020: $20,000, $40,000 and $10,000.

beats.text: Policies issued after July 1, 2020 default to a quarter-million per person and a half-million per accident for injuries, plus a skinny ten grand for property.
beats.say: Policies issued after July first, twenty twenty default to a quarter-million per person and a half-million per accident for injuries, plus a skinny ten grand for property.

beats.text: Lower injury limits take a signed DIFS form that explains the risks, and never go below $50,000 and $100,000.
beats.say: Lower injury limits take a signed D I F S form that explains the risks, and never go below fifty thousand dollars and one hundred thousand dollars.

beats.text: Older materials may show $20,000, $40,000 and $10,000: the rule before July 2, 2020.
beats.say: Older materials may show twenty thousand dollars, forty thousand dollars and ten thousand dollars: the rule before July second, twenty twenty.

scenes.src: MCL 500.3009(1),(5),(7),(8); DIFS FIS-PUB 6310; memory hook mn_auto-03; questions auto-001, auto-002

beats.text: I want the lowest injury limits Michigan allows. How do I get them?
beats.say: I want the lowest injury limits Michigan allows. How do I get them?

options.label: Sign the DIFS form for $50,000 and $100,000
options.win: Lower injury limits take the completed DIFS form, which explains the risks. $50,000 and $100,000 is the floor; property damage stays $10,000.

beats.text: Rosa reads the risks, signs, and gets $50,000 and $100,000.
beats.say: Rosa reads the risks, signs, and gets fifty thousand dollars and one hundred thousand dollars.

options.label: Ask for Dad's old $20,000 and $40,000
options.fail: $20,000 and $40,000 was the rule for policies before July 2, 2020. Today the lowest Rosa may choose is $50,000 and $100,000.

beats.text: Sorry, Rosa. Those limits ended in July 2020.
beats.say: Sorry, Rosa. Those limits ended in July twenty twenty.

options.label: Skip the form and let Dana sort it out
options.fail: Lower limits need the completed DIFS form. With no effective choice, the $250,000 and $500,000 defaults apply.

beats.text: Rosa never completes the form. Blank form, blank check: big defaults.
beats.say: Rosa never completes the form. Blank form, blank check: big defaults.

reveal.text: Lower limits need the signed DIFS form. Blank form? Big defaults.

(one limit for injuries and property damage together)

beats.text: Saturdays, Rosa drives for a ride-share app. Michigan sets special minimums.
beats.say: Saturdays, Rosa drives for a ride-share app. Michigan sets special minimums.

beats.text: Logged on and available, no ride yet: at least $50,000 and $100,000 bodily injury and $25,000 property damage, plus PIP and PPI.
beats.say: Logged on and available, no ride yet: at least fifty thousand dollars and one hundred thousand dollars bodily injury and twenty-five thousand dollars property damage, plus P I P and P P I.

beats.say: On a prearranged ride: at least one million dollars combined single limit, plus P I P and P P I.

draw.text: Can I borrow it? I have a date!

beats.text: Rosa agreed to it: her policy won't cover her brother Leo behind the wheel. He's a named excluded driver. Now Leo wants the car. What does Rosa say?
beats.say: Rosa agreed to it: her policy won't cover her brother Leo behind the wheel. He's a named excluded driver. Now Leo wants the car. What does Rosa say?

options.label: Sure! I'm the policyholder, so we're covered
options.fail: In Michigan, when a named excluded driver drives, all liability coverage is void: no one is insured. And he gets no PIP.

beats.text: Crunch! Leo rear-ends a pickup. No one is insured for liability, and Leo gets no PIP.
beats.say: Crunch! Leo rear-ends a pickup. No one is insured for liability, and Leo gets no P I P.

options.label: No. I'll drive you to your date myself
options.win: Rosa isn't excluded, so her coverage applies while she drives. Only the excluded driver at the wheel voids it.

beats.text: Rosa drives. Leo rides along, embarrassed. Her coverage works as usual.
beats.say: Rosa drives. Leo rides along, embarrassed. Her coverage works as usual.

options.label: OK, but I'll ride along to keep you careful
options.fail: Riding along changes nothing. While the named excluded person drives, all liability coverage is void.

beats.text: Rosa rides shotgun. Doesn't matter: Leo drives, so no one is insured for liability.
beats.say: Rosa rides shotgun. Doesn't matter: Leo drives, so no one is insured for liability.

reveal.text: In Michigan, an excluded driver at the wheel voids all liability coverage, and he gets no PIP.
reveal.say: In Michigan, an excluded driver at the wheel voids all liability coverage, and he gets no P I P.

scenes.q: Rosa is giving a prearranged ride through a ride-share app. Michigan requires the liability coverage for that ride to be at least:

$250,000 and $500,000 bodily injury, plus $10,000 property damage

beats.say: Pop quiz: Rosa is on a prearranged ride. What's the minimum?

scenes.title: Rosa rents a car: is she an owner?
scenes.plain: In Michigan no-fault, the owner or registrant must insure the car. Anyone renting or using it for more than 30 days counts as an owner.
scenes.example: Rosa rents a car for one week while hers is fixed: not an owner. Renting it for 60 days would make her one.
scenes.exam: Another 30-day rule: a nonresident may drive a car not registered here an aggregate of 30 days per calendar year without Michigan no-fault.

beats.text: With her car in the shop, Rosa rents one for a week. Is she an owner? Owners include anyone renting or using a car over 30 days.
beats.say: With her car in the shop, Rosa rents one for a week. Is she an owner? Owners include anyone renting or using a car over thirty days.

beats.text: One week? Not an owner. Sixty days? Owner.
beats.say: One week? Not an owner. Sixty days? Owner.

beats.text: Another 30: a nonresident may drive a car not registered here up to 30 days in all per calendar year, without Michigan no-fault.
beats.say: Another thirty: a nonresident may drive a car not registered here up to thirty days in all per calendar year, without Michigan no-fault.

scenes.title: Rear-ended near Traverse City: who pays Rosa's PIP?

draw.text: Empty table? Michigan Assigned Claims Plan
Renter hurts someone? Rental of 30 days or less, company not negligent: liable as owner up to $20,000 and $40,000

beats.text: Near Traverse City, a driver rear-ends Rosa's rental.
beats.say: Near Traverse City, a driver rear-ends Rosa's rental.

beats.text: Ow! His insurer pays my PIP, right?
beats.say: Ow! His insurer pays my P I P, right?

beats.text: No. PIP is no-fault. Kitchen-table rule: first, the policies on your own table. Yours, your spouse's, or a relative's who lives with you.
beats.say: No. P I P is no-fault. Kitchen-table rule: first, the policies on your own table. Yours, your spouse's, or a relative's who lives with you.

beats.text: So Rosa's own insurer pays. Key exceptions: hurt in your employer's vehicle? Its insurer pays. Motorcyclist hit by a car? The car owner's insurer first.
beats.say: So Rosa's own insurer pays. Key exceptions: hurt in your employer's vehicle? Its insurer pays. Motorcyclist hit by a car? The car owner's insurer first.

beats.text: Nothing on the table? Under the 2019 amendments, the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan.
beats.say: Nothing on the table? Under the twenty nineteen amendments, the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan.

beats.text: Another rental rule: on rentals of 30 days or less, if the renter's driving hurts someone, a rental company that wasn't negligent is liable as owner only up to $20,000 per person and $40,000 per accident. Same numbers as the old limits, but still the law.
beats.say: Another rental rule: on rentals of thirty days or less, if the renter's driving hurts someone, a rental company that wasn't negligent is liable as owner only up to twenty thousand dollars per person and forty thousand dollars per accident. Same numbers as the old limits, but still the law.

scenes.title: Who pays PIP first?
scenes.src: MCL 500.3114(1),(3)-(5); 500.3115, as amended by 2019 PA 21; questions auto-026 to auto-029, auto-047

items.text: Rosa, hurt in her one-week rental
items.why: A one-week renter isn't an owner. Her own policy pays first.

items.text: Rosa's coworker, hurt driving the company's truck
items.why: An employee in a vehicle owned or registered by the employer: that vehicle's insurer pays.

items.text: A Lansing resident hit while walking; no policy, lives alone
items.why: No own or household policy: under the 2019 amendments, the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan.

items.text: Teen passenger, no policy, lives with his insured mom
items.why: A relative living in the same household: his mom's policy pays first.

items.text: Jen, hurt driving her employer's van; she has her own policy
items.why: The employer's vehicle rule comes first: that vehicle's insurer pays, not her own policy.

items.text: Hurt riding in a friend's car; no own or household policy
items.why: Under the 2019 amendments, an occupant with no own or household policy claims through the Assigned Claims Plan.

beats.text: Your turn: who pays each person's PIP first?
beats.say: Your turn: who pays each person's P I P first?

reveal.text: Employer's vehicle? Its insurer. Motorcyclist hit by a car? The car owner's insurer. Otherwise, usually your own kitchen table. Nothing there? The Assigned Claims Plan.
reveal.say: Employer's vehicle? Its insurer. Motorcyclist hit by a car? The car owner's insurer. Otherwise, usually your own kitchen table. Nothing there? The Assigned Claims Plan.

scenes.title: Michigan's safety net: the placement facility

draw.text: MAIPF: Michigan Automobile Insurance Placement Facility
Nobody would insure me the ordinary way.

spots.label: Every auto insurer
spots.text: Every insurer authorized to write auto insurance in Michigan must take part in the Michigan Automobile Insurance Placement Facility.

spots.label: Guaranteed coverage
spots.text: Walt couldn't get auto insurance through ordinary methods. The facility exists to guarantee coverage for people like him.

spots.label: Yearly notice
spots.text: At least once each year, facility insureds must be told the standards for buying insurance in the voluntary (regular) market.

spots.label: Runs the Assigned Claims Plan
spots.text: The facility runs the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan, where people with no own or household policy claim PIP.

spots.label: Notice within 1 year
spots.text: Claiming through the plan? Notify the facility within 1 year after the accident.

spots.label: $250,000 medical cap
spots.text: Medical benefits through the plan are generally capped at $250,000.

beats.text: Who runs that plan? The Michigan Automobile Insurance Placement Facility, or MAIPF. Its main job? Meet Rosa's neighbor Walt.
beats.say: Who runs that plan? The Michigan Automobile Insurance Placement Facility, or M A I P F. Its main job? Meet Rosa's neighbor Walt.

beats.text: Nobody would insure me the ordinary way.
beats.say: Nobody would insure me the ordinary way.

beats.text: Tap the glowing spots.
beats.say: Tap the glowing spots.

reveal.text: Every auto insurer must take part. It guarantees coverage for people like Walt and runs the plan. Claimants tell it within a year after the accident.
reveal.say: Every auto insurer must take part. It guarantees coverage for people like Walt and runs the plan. Claimants tell it within a year after the accident.

scenes.title: Chapter 32 auto cancellations: the 55-day speed limit
scenes.src: MCL 500.3204(2), 3208, 3212, 3220, 3224, 3230; MCL 500.2123; adapted from memory hook mn_auto-18; question auto-044

draw.text: Essential Insurance Act (not nonpayment): 30 days, 20 in first 55
First 55 days: may cancel for unacceptable risk. No appeal.
After day 55 or renewal: only a final license suspension or revocation
Cancel: at least 20 days ahead, reasons, bold 7-day appeal notice
Nonrenew: first-class mail, at least 20 days ahead. Not a cancellation

beats.text: Ninety days in, Rosa's insurer wants out. Michigan's Chapter 32 posts a speed limit: 55.
beats.say: Ninety days in, Rosa's insurer wants out. Michigan's Chapter thirty-two posts a speed limit: fifty-five.

beats.text: In the first 55 days, it may cancel for unacceptable risk, no appeal. After that, or at once on a renewal, only for a final license suspension or revocation: the named insured's, or a household or customary driver's.
beats.say: In the first fifty-five days, it may cancel for unacceptable risk, no appeal. After that, or at once on a renewal, only for a final license suspension or revocation: the named insured's, or a household or customary driver's.

beats.text: Cancel by certified mail, at least 20 days ahead, with reasons and a 7-day appeal notice. Nonrenew by normal first-class mail, same 20 days: not a cancellation.
beats.say: Cancel by certified mail, at least twenty days ahead, with reasons and a seven-day appeal notice. Nonrenew by normal first-class mail, same twenty days: not a cancellation.

beats.text: Nonpayment is outside Chapter 32. Watch out: a separate law, the Essential Insurance Act, requires 30 days' notice for reasons other than nonpayment, or 20 in the first 55. Check the statute named.
beats.say: Nonpayment is outside Chapter thirty-two. Watch out: a separate law, the Essential Insurance Act, requires thirty days' notice for reasons other than nonpayment, or twenty in the first fifty-five. Check the statute named.

draw.text: How do we cancel this one?

beats.text: Day 90: Jay, Rosa's roommate who drives her car daily, has his license suspended, and it's final. Under Chapter 32, how should the insurer cancel?
beats.say: Day ninety: Jay, Rosa's roommate who drives her car daily, has his license suspended, and it's final. Under Chapter thirty-two, how should the insurer cancel?

options.label: Cancel, calling Rosa an unacceptable risk
options.fail: Unacceptable risk is a reason only in the first 55 days. After that, Chapter 32 allows only a final license suspension or revocation.

beats.text: Too late. After day 55, unacceptable risk is off the table.
beats.say: Too late. After day fifty-five, unacceptable risk is off the table.

options.label: Cancel over Jay: first-class, 20 days ahead
options.fail: First-class mail at least 20 days ahead is the nonrenewal rule. A Chapter 32 cancellation goes by certified mail.

beats.text: Wrong envelope. First-class mail is for nonrenewal. A cancellation goes certified.
beats.say: Wrong envelope. First-class mail is for nonrenewal. A cancellation goes certified.

options.label: Cancel over Jay: certified, 20 days ahead
options.win: Under Chapter 32, after day 55, a final license suspension is a valid reason. Certified, at least 20 days ahead, reasons, bold 7-day appeal notice.

beats.text: Certified, 20 days ahead, with the reason and a bold 7-day appeal notice.
beats.say: Certified, twenty days ahead, with the reason and a bold seven-day appeal notice.

draw.text: Reason: Jay's final suspension. You may appeal within 7 days of mailing.

options.label: Cancel over Jay: certified, 5 days ahead
options.fail: A Chapter 32 cancellation notice must be mailed at least 20 days before it takes effect.

beats.text: Too short! 20 days, minimum.
beats.say: Too short! Twenty days, minimum.

reveal.text: Chapter 32: cancel certified, nonrenew normal first-class, both at least 20 days ahead.
reveal.say: Chapter thirty-two: cancel certified, nonrenew normal first-class, both at least twenty days ahead.
